Calculate the point where the ellipse $\frac{(x+3)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-6)^{2}}{36}=1$ intercepts the $x$-axis.

The $x$-intercept is $($

{{field-2}}$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercept, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+3)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-6)^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+3)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(0-6)^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+3)^{2}}{9}+\frac{36}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+3)^{2}}{9}+1 & =1 \\ \frac{(x+3)^{2}}{9} & =0 \\ (x+3)^{2} & =0 \\ x+3 & =0 \\ x & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $x$-axis at the point $(-3,0).$
